target.title: fix(telegram): preserve authored file-reference links
target.body: Closes #105679 ## What Problem This Solves Telegram's Markdown formatter treated any authored link whose visible label matched a supported file-like hostname as if it came from MarkdownIt's automatic linkifier. For example, `[README.md](https://README.md)` was indistinguishable from a plain `README.md` reference and the authored anchor was silently replaced with `README.md`. The supported suppression extensions currently include `.md`, `.go`, `.py`, `.pl`, `.sh`, `.am`, `.at`, `.be`, and `.cc`. `.ts` is not in that set, so `main.ts` is not a valid before/after reproducer for this bug. ## Why This Change Was Made Markdown Core now keeps MarkdownIt's `linkify` provenance as private renderer metadata instead of adding a field to the public `MarkdownLinkSpan` contract. The fact is copied through clamping, slicing, table transforms, render-boundary splitting, and render-aware chunk coalescing. `renderMarkdownWithMarkers` exposes only a renderer-specific `{ origin: "authored" | "linkify" }` context while evaluating a link. Telegram suppresses a file-like link only when that context says it came from MarkdownIt's `linkify` rule. Markdown/IR output then wraps remaining plain file references without trying to infer provenance again from rendered anchors. Explicit Markdown links therefore remain anchors, while the public raw-HTML helper keeps its default defensive de-linkification behavior because raw HTML does not carry trustworthy parser provenance. The branch was rebuilt on `main` after the Markdown IR and Telegram renderer refactors, removing the prior merge conflict and picking up the upstream fixes for the two unrelated CI failures seen on the previous head. GitHub currently reports the PR as mergeable; repository policy treats subsequent moving-`main` drift as advisory unless an actual conflict appears, so the proven head remains stable. ## User Impact Intentional Telegram links whose labels resemble supported file names keep their destinations, while plain file references such as `README.md` continue to render as code and avoid unwanted registrar previews. Existing direct-HTML compatibility behavior is preserved. ## Evidence - Head: `0d6ac6385ca8f5538a31e2fb3a8f58c1de2ad937`. - `git diff --check` passed. - Focused Markdown Core coverage checks public span shape plus renderer provenance through parsing/clamping, slicing, and table rendering. - Telegram formatter coverage checks authored-link preservation for a supported `.md` label, automatic file-reference suppression, mixed authored/plain output, chunked output, the Bot API 10.2 rich-block path introduced on current `main`, and existing raw-HTML de-linkification behavior. - Post-rebase hosted CI run [`29411581760`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29411581760) is fully green: 53 successful jobs, 12 scope skips, and no failures. This includes `check-test-types`, `check-dependencies`, lint/format, the plugin SDK surface budget, every Node test shard, build artifacts, prod types, guards, and the aggregate `openclaw/ci-gate`. - The previous head's two unrelated failures were fixed upstream by #107987 (`session-history-state` test typing) and #107977 (serialized hooks process bootstraps); rebasing picked up both fixes. - Initial Mantis run `29396726601` showed that `main.ts` has no baseline/candidate delta because `.ts` is not a supported suppression extension. - Corrected Mantis run `29401877063` passed against baseline `ad1071bcd0` and candidate `9be0456f81`. The [proof comment](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105911#issuecomment-4978225456) contains paired native Telegram Desktop screenshots, GIFs, and MP4s; the evidence manifest marks both lanes `pass`, candidate `fixed: true`, and overall `pass: true`. - The Mantis proof job itself succeeded, including manifest validation, artifact upload, and PR evidence publication. The workflow's red conclusion comes only from a separate `Clear Mantis command reaction` cleanup job receiving a 403 while removing the eyes reaction.
